title: Company-wide policies and processes (access & permissions, change management, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the internal template library. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers responsible for operational compliance and process execution.

Scope and ownership:
- Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors operating on Redwood systems or acting on behalf of Redwood in any capacity.
- Primary owners: People Ops (policy maintenance), Security & Compliance (access and data controls), Finance (procurement & expense rules), Legal (vendor contracts), Eng-SRE & Eng-Infra (technical change processes).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review or ad-hoc when regulatory or business changes require updates.

1) Access & permissions
Purpose: Provide clear, auditable controls for granting, modifying, and revoking access to Redwood systems and data.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: Grant the minimum set of permissions required for the role or task.
- Role-based access: Use defined roles (e.g., eng-readonly, eng-deployer, finance-admin) rather than granting ad-hoc permissions.
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevated access: Temporary privilege escalation must be approved and logged.
- Auditability: All access changes must be recordable in our access management system (Okta / IAM logs).

Process:
1. Access request: Submit an access request via the internal Access Request form (Confluence link) with justification and list of affected resources.
2. Approval: Requests require approval from the resource owner and the requester's manager. For high-sensitivity resources (production infra, customer data stores, KMS/HSM), Security must also approve.
3. Provisioning: Provisioning is automated where possible. Manual changes must be logged in the change ticket.
4. Periodic review: Managers must review active access for their direct reports quarterly; Security will run a company-wide access audit biannually.
5. Offboarding: On termination or role change, IT/People Ops must revoke access within 4 hours for contractors and 24 hours for employees.

Roles and examples: (table inline)
- eng-readonly: Read access to non-production logs and dashboards.
- eng-deployer: CI/CD deployment permissions for staging and selected production services.
- infra-admin: Cluster and network admin, requires Security approval.

Escalations and exceptions:
- Exceptions: Any exception must be captured in the Risk & Exceptions registry with an owner, expiration date, and compensating controls.
- Emergency access: Use JIT process; all emergency sessions must be recorded and reviewed within 72 hours.

2) Change management
Purpose: Ensure safe, auditable, and low-risk changes to production and supporting systems.

Scope: Software deployments, infrastructure changes (IaC), network updates, configuration changes to supporting services (databases, queues), and schema changes affecting production data.

Change categories and approvals:
- Standard change: Routine, well-documented, low-risk (no separate approval required; follow runbook).
- Minor change: Low-medium risk; requires manager approval and runbook sign-off.
- Major change: High-risk (schema changes, failover, infra upgrades); require SRE & Product approval and a rollback plan.
- Emergency change: Unplanned changes to mitigate production incidents; document in postmortem and retro.

Process steps (numbered):
1. Create a change ticket in the change tracker (JIRA project: CHG). Include impact assessment, rollback plan, runbook, owners, scheduled window, and validation steps.
2. Runbook validation: Peer review required for all non-standard changes.
3. Approval gating: Major changes require SRE on-call and Product manager approval.
4. Deployment: Execute during approved maintenance window; use feature flags where possible.
5. Validation: Post-change validation checklist executed by owner.
6. Close ticket: Attach logs, monitoring snapshots, and update documentation.

SLOs and timing:
- Change review turnaround: 24 hours for minor changes, 72 hours for major changes.
- Emergency rollback target: 30 minutes for critical outages.

3) Data management
Purpose: Protect customer and internal data integrity, confidentiality, and availability.

Data classification:
- Public: No restrictions; can be published.
- Internal: Internal use only; not customer-sensitive.
- Confidential: Customer data, secrets, PII, or regulated data. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, strict access controls, and audit logging.

Storage and handling rules:
- Encryption: All Confidential data must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Backups: Data backup policies for production services; retention and RTO/RPO defined per service in the Service Catalog.
- Masking & redaction: Use masking for logs and developer tools; do not include confidential data in error reports or dashboards.

Data retention and deletion:
- Retention schedules: Defined per data class in Data Retention matrix (link to registry).
- Deletion requests: Follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) process in Legal/Compliance.

Data access reviews and monitoring:
- Quarterly reviews for systems holding Confidential data.
- Continuous monitoring for anomalous access patterns; alerts routed to Security.

4) Procurement & expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing and expense reimbursement to control spend, ensure compliance, and provide clear ownership.

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- <= $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,001–$25,000: Department head approval + Finance notification.
- > $25,000: VP approval + Procurement/Finance involvement and legal review for vendor contracts.

POs and preferred vendors:
- Use Purchase Orders (POs) for all purchases > $5,000.
- Preferred vendor list maintained by Finance; use preferred contracts where available.

Expense policy (brief):
- Employees must submit expense reports within 30 days.
- Receipts required for all expenses >= $25.
- Travel: Follow Travel policy section for booking classes, per diems, and approvals.

Procurement process (steps):
1. Requestor submits a Purchase Request form with justification and estimated cost.
2. Manager approves and routes to Finance/Procurement.
3. Finance verifies budget; Procurement coordinates vendor terms.
4. Legal reviews contracts for new vendors or > $25k commitments.
5. Finance issues PO and approves payment terms.

5) Vendor management
Purpose: Ensure consistent onboarding, risk assessment, and ongoing monitoring of vendors providing services to Redwood.

Vendor lifecycle:
- Selection: Use RFP/RFI for strategic vendors > $50k/year.
- Risk assessment: Security questionnaire and privacy review for any vendor accessing Redwood data or networks.
- Contracting: Legal must sign off on standard terms; Security reviews SOC/ISO reports or equivalent.
- Onboarding: Assign vendor owner, configure least-privilege access, and schedule architecture/integration review.
- Ongoing monitoring: Quarterly reviews for high-risk vendors; annual security evidence refresh for vendors with access to Confidential data.

Vendor exit and offboarding:
- Offboarding checklist: Revoke credentials, remove network access, retrieve assets, confirm data deletion, and close contracts.
- Data return/destruction: Terms must be included in contract; Finance/Legal to validate compliance.

6) Travel policy
Purpose: Provide clear guidance on allowable travel, booking, approvals, safety, and expense reimbursement.

Key rules:
- Approvals: All travel requires manager pre-approval via Travel Request form. International travel requires People Ops notification and documented itinerary.
- Booking: Use approved travel portal (preferred vendor) for flights and hotels. Use economy class for flights < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Lodging: Mid-range hotels on the approved list; avoid extended-stay options unless approved.
- Per diem and meals: Follow regional per diem table (link). Receipts required for single meal expenses >= $75.
- Safety: Register international trips with People Ops; consult the Travel Safety guide for high-risk geographies.

COVID / Health exceptions: Follow local guidance and People Ops advisories; if quarantine impacts return, contact People Ops immediately for support.

7) Internal templates and forms
Content: Centralized templates for purchase requests, access requests, change tickets, vendor onboarding checklist, travel request, expense report, and postmortem template.

Location: Templates live in Confluence Templates Library (link) and must be used for all formal requests.

Template governance:
- Owners: Each template has an owner (document footer) responsible for updates.
- Versioning: Update the template header with the revision date and change summary.
- Exceptions: Temporary or project-specific templates require People Ops or document owner approval and must be stored in project docs with a cross-reference to the canonical template.

Related references and links:
- Access Request form (Confluence link)
- Change ticket template (CHG JIRA)
- Data Retention matrix (Data Governance page)
- Procurement request form (Finance portal)
- Vendor security questionnaire (Security drive)
- Travel portal and per diem table (Travel guide)
- Templates Library (Confluence templates)

Appendix: Escalation contacts and SLAs:
- Emergency security incident: security@redwood-inference.com, on-call security duty (pager)
- Procurement escalation: procurement@redwood-inference.com (response SLA: 24 business hours)
- Access revocation SLA on termination: 4 hours for contractors, 24 hours for employees
